**Melde** — the time is four steel wires standing on a shaker rail, bent into numerals and sing; the seconds are a sweep generator climbing a frequency scale, and each wire swells as the sweep crosses its own resonance mark.

How the time is the mechanism: every digit is one continuous bend of wire (the 4, 8 and 9 cross themselves, as a real bend must), and it's drawn as a vibrating wire rather than a stroke — pinched to a hairline at each node of its own standing wave, swollen into a lens at every antinode, with the lobes crawling because the strobe sits slightly off the drive. The mode number is a property of the numeral, so a 1 rings in 3 lobes and an 8 in 7. Two systems: the minutes stand on the rail, big and loud; the hours sit up on the beam with a vice jaw gripping each foot, so they stay fine and quiet, because a clamp damps.

The turn: on the flyback the drive slams back down the scale, the changing wires are pulled taut into shimmering spindles, then the new bend unfurls out of each one from the welded foot upward (~1.4 s minutes, ~2.4 s on the hour, when the jaws also ride up and all four wires re-bend before the vice drops back and bites).

Renders — all re-rendered against the final file:
- `out/chladni-opus5.png` (hero, 10:09:50)
- `out/chladni-opus5-digits.png` (the ten-digit set)
- `out/chladni-opus5-turn.png` (sheet across the 10:09 → 10:10 turn)
- `out/chladni-opus5-hour.png` (sheet across 10:59 → 11:00)
- `out/chladni-opus5.gif`, `out/chladni-opus5-hour.gif`

`node tools/check.mjs --design chladni-opus5` → **PASS**: worst frame 0.83 ms, 1024 RAM bytes, 0 frames over the bus budget, 20.2 % of the glass lit on average, hottest pixel ~1.8 years to 50 %.

Two rounds of critique changed real things. Round one killed the morph chimeras (every glyph's control list now starts at the foot so the front climbs the wire the way a transient actually does), replaced a clamp bar that was cutting the hour digits in half with two vice jaws outside them, and turned a dithered "texture" background into a single-pixel generator trace. Round two was the transition: a travelling front left the wire half one numeral and half another, and halfway between a 5 and a 0 is a readable shape of its own — the hour show was passing through something that looked like "F F". Routing the morph through a taut spindle fixed it structurally, and the spindle had to be made to shimmer, because a crisp vertical stroke is itself a numeral.

Honest weakest point: the bottom-left machine cluster. The post, beam, gusset ribs, jaws and exciter coil crowd into about 55 x 25 px, and at 1x they read as a bank of bars before they read as a bench — you can tell it's apparatus, but not which part is which. The right margin (x 114–126) is also nearly empty, carrying only the far end post, so the composition leans left of where the hero is.
